data.sourceTitle: Judaism (Section A) — June 2020 — GCSE Religious Studies Overview
data.sourcePassage: This pack covers the AQA GCSE Religious Studies examination for Judaism (Section A), sitting: June 2020 — GCSE Religious Studies. The paper is divided into two sections: Beliefs and Practices. In the Beliefs section, students are expected to demonstrate knowledge of core Judaism (Section A) teachings, explain how those beliefs influence followers today, and evaluate significant statements using religious evidence. In the Practices section, students explore how Judaism (Section A) is lived out in worship, festivals, community life, and ethical action. Each section follows the same five-question structure: a 1-mark multiple choice question, a 2-mark 'give two' question, a 4-mark 'explain two' question, a 5-mark 'explain and refer to scripture' question, and a 12-mark evaluate question worth additional SPaG marks. One of the key evaluative questions for June 2020 — GCSE Religious Studies asks students to consider: ‘For Jews, justice is the most important of the moral principles.’. This requires understanding arguments on both sides before reaching a justified conclusion. Students should practise writing well-structured answers that include specific religious teachings, use accurate terminology, and demonstrate understanding of how beliefs shape the lives of believers today.
